title: Defensive tools
description: CyberChef, REMnux/FlareVM and safe lab setup.

1.title: CyberChef: the Swiss Army knife of analysis
1.body:
## GCHQ's "operations cylinder"

**CyberChef** (gchq.github.io/CyberChef, runs offline in your browser) chains
operations: the output of each one feeds the next.

```text
Input: RkxBR3s=  →  [From Base64]  →  [ROT13]  →  FLAG{...}
```

Star operations for everyday work:
- **From/To Base64, Hex, URL** — the usual decoders.
- **ROT13, XOR** — challenges and simple malware.
- **Extract IPs / URLs / emails** — from a log or a dirty binary.
- **Magic** — it guesses the chain of operations for you! (try it: paste the ROT13+base64
  from your previous rooms and click Magic).

For an analyst: examining headers, decoding phishing payloads, extracting IOCs
from a log. For a CTF: 50% of the "decoding" challenges.

It needs no installation: download the HTML and it works offline (ideal for evidence
you don't want to expose to the internet).

2.title: REMnux, FlareVM and the safe lab
2.body:
## Ready-made distributions

- **REMnux**: Ubuntu loaded with tools for malware and evidence analysis:
  decoders, PDF/Office analyzers, network sniffing, IOC extraction
  scripts.
- **FlareVM**: the same but on Windows (a PS> installer that turns a VM into a
  reverse engineering lab: debuggers, PE dissectors, decompilers).

## The golden rule of the lab

```text
Analysis VM  ←→  host-only network  (NEVER bridged to your LAN)
```

Malware is detonated in the VM with the network isolated (or with INetSim/FakeNet simulating
the internet to see what it "calls"). Snapshots BEFORE detonating: analyze → restore →
repeat. An analyst without snapshots ends up reinstalling everything far too often.

## Closing the path's circle

You now know both sides: attacking (recon, exploits, offensive tooling) and defending (SOC,
logs, SIEM, analysis). The last module of the path connects all of this with YOUR career.

herramientas-defensivas-t02-q01.hint: It's based on Ubuntu and comes loaded with tools to analyze samples and evidence.

options.b: A commercial antivirus for Linux servers
options.c: A GCHQ web tool for decoding data
options.d: An installer that turns a Windows VM into a reversing lab

herramientas-defensivas-t02-q02.prompt: Where should dangerous malware ALWAYS be analyzed?
herramientas-defensivas-t02-q02.hint: An isolated machine, with no access to your real network.

options.a: On your work laptop, with up-to-date antivirus
options.b: In a dedicated, isolated virtual machine (host-only network)

herramientas-defensivas-t02-q03.prompt: Which kit is the equivalent of REMnux but for Windows (Win32 malware analysis)?
herramientas-defensivas-t02-q03.hint: It installs on top of a Windows VM; flare.
